name: Distressed debt investing
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Forced Selling and Complexity
caseLead: Distressed debt investing seeks returns when stressed bonds trade below the value expected from refinancing, asset sales or restructuring. Forced sales by funds with rating restrictions can create these discounts, while legal complexity, sanctions and the time required for restructuring limit the number of buyers.
caseRest: Debt recoveries can fall below expectations if the issuer's asset value declines or legal proceedings weaken creditors' claims. Indicative results show an 11.8% annual return with 12.2% volatility, but the strategy’s negative 0.7 return skew and 30.0% worst fall show that losses can be concentrated. Illiquidity compounds this risk because bid-ask spreads widen during defaults, preventing positions from being reduced without accepting a substantial discount.
figNote: Each card shows the highest US high-yield option-adjusted spread during the episode, rounded to the nearest 10 basis points. The spread measures the additional yield over US Treasuries after allowing for embedded options, so a higher figure indicates greater default and liquidity risk.

events.title: Funding stress cuts expected recoveries
events.text: The financial crisis closed refinancing markets and reduced the value of assets supporting leveraged companies, pushing high-yield spreads above 2,000 basis points. The strategy lost because expected recoveries fell while forced selling drove distressed bond prices below executable values.

events.title: Policy support restores restructuring values
events.text: Government support for banks and the restructuring of major US carmakers improved access to funding as high-yield spreads began to fall. The strategy gained because surviving companies refinanced debt and completed restructurings at recoveries above crisis prices.

events.title: Euro crisis restricts corporate refinancing
events.text: The euro-area sovereign crisis weakened banks and restricted credit to leveraged companies, lifting US high-yield spreads to about 910 basis points. The strategy lost because refinancing risk increased and buyers demanded larger discounts for illiquid claims.

events.title: Oil defaults create uneven recoveries
events.text: The oil price decline drove US energy producers into default and lifted high-yield spreads close to 890 basis points. Results were mixed because unsecured claims lost value, while senior secured debt bought near liquidation value later produced strong recoveries.

events.title: Shutdowns reduce cash flow and liquidity
events.text: Pandemic restrictions removed revenue from travel, retail and energy companies while high-yield spreads rose above 1,000 basis points. The strategy suffered its worst loss because recovery estimates fell rapidly and dealer liquidity weakened across distressed bonds.

events.title: Federal Reserve support reopens credit markets
events.text: Federal Reserve credit facilities restored market access for many speculative-grade issuers as high-yield spreads retreated from their March peak. The strategy gained because refinancing reduced near-term defaults and raised the expected value of stressed bonds.

instrument: US and European stressed corporate bonds, defaulted claims and restructuring debt
rules: Debt bought at a material discount to estimated recovery value; seniority, collateral and legal jurisdiction assessed before entry; issuer and sector limits applied
costs: Estimated bid-ask spreads, legal expenses, advisory fees and trading commissions deducted
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from recovery discounts to downside control

legs.instrument: Senior secured and unsecured corporate bonds
legs.purpose: Captures recovery through refinancing or asset sales

legs.instrument: Bonds and bank debt in restructuring
legs.purpose: Captures distributions above the purchase price
Earns contractual income with priority over existing claims
Reduces broad spread and recession risk
Funds legal costs and new distressed opportunities

entry: Market price at least 20% below a conservative estimate of recovery value
size: Maximum 5% per issuer and 20% per sector at cost
exit: Position closed when recovery value is reached or restructuring proceeds are distributed
stop: Position reviewed for exit if estimated recovery value falls by 20%
marketWatch: The key indicators are default rates, maturity schedules, bank lending standards, high-yield spreads and prices for loans that share the same collateral. Upcoming earnings, refinancing deadlines and court rulings will determine whether stressed issuers can preserve enterprise value. Sanctions, tariff changes and government support can also alter asset values or creditors’ legal rights.

favourable.heading: Refinancing markets reopen
favourable.text: Improving credit access favours the strategy because stressed issuers can refinance near-term maturities before weak liquidity becomes insolvency. Federal Reserve support in 2020 reopened bond markets and raised the value of debt bought during the March sell-off.

favourable.heading: Recoveries exceed market prices
favourable.text: Stable asset values favour the strategy when secured claims trade below the proceeds available from collateral sales or a reorganisation. Several energy restructurings after the 2016 oil slump produced gains for senior creditors even when equity holders were largely wiped out.

favourable.heading: Forced selling creates discounts
favourable.text: Downgrades and index removal favour the strategy because constrained investors sell without waiting for the restructuring value to emerge. During the 2009 recovery, debt bought from forced sellers rose as refinancing markets reopened and default expectations declined.

adverse.heading: Enterprise value falls sharply
adverse.text: Falling revenue and asset prices hurt the strategy because less value remains available for creditors after secured claims and restructuring costs are paid. Pandemic shutdowns in March 2020 sharply reduced expected recoveries in travel, retail and energy debt.

adverse.heading: Proceedings delay creditor payments
adverse.text: Long insolvency proceedings hurt returns because legal expenses rise and capital remains unavailable for new opportunities. Puerto Rico’s restructuring showed how litigation and competing creditor claims can delay distributions for several years.

adverse.heading: Policy weakens creditor rights
adverse.text: Government intervention hurts the strategy when sanctions, emergency laws or political priorities restrict asset transfers and change the treatment of claims. Sanctions on Russian companies in 2022 reduced market access and complicated payments to foreign bondholders.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy’s estimated peak-to-trough return during each event, using changes in distressed bond prices, high-yield spreads and expected recoveries under the default portfolio rules. Each window runs from the last portfolio high before the shock to the subsequent low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn’s scenario engine projects changes in credit spreads, default probabilities, interest rates, sector cash flows and recovery values, then applies them to the strategy’s positions and credit hedge.
altTitle: Where Else Can Investors Find Credit Mispricing?

related.why: Trades defined corporate events and bears execution risk rather than waiting for a broad restructuring recovery.
Hedges convertible mispricing and bears model, funding and short-equity risk instead of outright recovery risk.
Earns income from short-maturity high-yield bonds and bears refinancing risk without relying on formal restructuring.
